title: Open-source licence
intro: First Move is open source. This page explains which licence covers the code, the documentation and the Quick Check methodology, what it allows, what it requires in return, and which parts are under other licences.

| Source code | {{license.name}} (`{{license.spdx}}`) |
| Documentation | {{license.name}} (`{{license.spdx}}`) |

sections.heading: Source code
body: The source code of First Move is published at [{{repo.url}}]({{repo.url}}) under the {{license.name}}. Its SPDX identifier is `{{license.spdx}}`. The licence text is in the [LICENSE]({{repo.licenseUrl}}) file of the repository, and the official text is at [{{license.url}}]({{license.url}}). The code is © {{copyright.year}} {{operator.name}}. Contributions remain the copyright of their authors, who license them on the same terms (see [Contributions](#contributions)).

If you distribute First Move or a work based on it, you must (Section 4):

You may add your own copyright notice to your changes and license them on other terms, as long as your use and distribution of First Move itself complies with the licence.

sections.heading: Quick Check methodology
body: The Quick Check methodology, meaning its equations, tables and default values, is derived from the AQC methodology supplied with the 5GDHC hackathon challenge. We publish it under the {{license.name}}, the same licence as the code, with the permission of its rights holders. Credit for the original methodology goes to its originators.

If you reuse or change the equations, tables or default values, the conditions under [Source code](#code) apply in the same way: pass on the licence and the attribution notices, and mark what you changed.

The methodology is a screening method. Its results are an initial indication, not a feasibility study and not engineering advice. They rest on simplified assumptions and must be refined. The calculations are deterministic: they follow the published equations and default tables and are not produced by AI.

sections.heading: Documentation
body: The documentation in the repository, including the pages under [Docs](/docs), is published under the {{license.name}} as well. You may copy, translate, adapt and republish it, also commercially, on the same conditions as the code: pass on the licence and the notices, and mark what you changed.

If you publish a modified version or run your own copy of the app, give it a different name and do not suggest that it is First Move or that we endorse it.

sections.heading: Third-party software
body: First Move is built on open-source packages by other authors. Each package stays under the licence its authors chose: the {{license.name}} of First Move does not change that licence, and the package licence governs the package. The table below lists the packages shipped with First Move, including the fonts, with the licence of each and a link to its project.

sections.heading: Fonts
body: First Move uses two typefaces: Archivo and IBM Plex Mono. They are licensed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (SPDX identifier `OFL-1.1`), not under the {{license.name}}. They are delivered with the `@fontsource` packages `@fontsource-variable/archivo` and `@fontsource/ibm-plex-mono`, which carry the licence texts. The fonts are served from this site, not from an external font service.

sections.heading: Contributions
body: You can contribute through the [repository]({{repo.url}}) on GitHub. GitHub's own terms apply to your use of that platform.

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution you intentionally submit for inclusion in First Move, such as code, documentation or changes to the methodology, is licensed under the {{license.name}}, without any additional terms or conditions (Section 5). You keep the copyright in your contribution. Submit only work you have the right to license on these terms.

We are not obliged to accept, review or merge a contribution. The [Terms of Use](/terms#contributions) set out the further rules for contributions, including how we handle AI-assisted feedback, issues and pull requests.

sections.heading: Contact
body: For questions about the licence, permissions or attribution, write to [{{operator.emailHuman}}](mailto:{{operator.emailHuman}}). Please do not send licence or legal questions to {{operator.emailAgent}}: that mailbox is answered by an AI system.
